title: Enzymatic Release of N-Glycans from Monoclonal Antibodies Using PNGase F
author: Kimmy Park

steps.title: Denature antibody
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mg monoclonal antibody with 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate to obtain a 1 mg/mL solution. Add either 4 µL of 40 mM DTT or 4 µL of denaturing buffer (40 mM DTT, 0.5 % SDS). Heat the mixture at 100 °C for 12 minutes to fully denature the protein.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 1 mg/mL antibody solution in 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Add 4 µL of 40 mM DTT (or 4 µL denaturing buffer containing 40 mM DTT and 0.5 % SDS).

steps.title: Cool sample
steps.instruction: Immediately place the tube on ice or in a freezer for 5 minutes to dissipate residual heat.

steps.title: Neutralize SDS (if present)
steps.instruction: If SDS was included in the denaturation step, add 4 µL of 1 % NP‑40 to neutralize SDS and prevent PNGase F inhibition.

steps.title: Add PNGase F
steps.instruction: Add 2–4 µL of PNGase F (or the equivalent recommended enzyme units) to the reaction mixture.

steps.title: Collect and dry glycans
steps.instruction: After the PNGase F incubation, collect the reaction mixture containing released N‑glycans and residual protein. Lyophilize or speed‑vac to dryness if preparing for downstream cleanup/labeling, or store the dried sample at –80 °C.
